raw_response:
I am getting on in years and my back is not as strong as it was, but this land is what I know. My family has grown winter wheat and summer maize on this same ground for as long as I can remember. My husband's parents did it, we did it, and I will do it again this year. Eight mu, same as always.

For the **winter wheat** — it is already in the ground from last October, so now in spring I must manage it through to the June harvest. I will water it at jointing and again before heading, like I always do. My neighbor told me to spray once for aphids. I use the same fertilizer amounts my husband always used before he got sick — we buy urea and the phosphate in bags from the village shop.

For the **summer maize** — right after wheat comes off in June, I will hire the rotary tiller to come through so I can plant quickly. Maize is fast money and I know how to manage it. I will plant hybrid seed because the village supply station sells that now and the yield is better. If it does not rain in August I will pump water once from the well.

I will not try anything new this year. I am 59, I have no schooling, and I cannot afford a bad harvest. I do what I know.
